note: One entry per CONFIRMED fix. Audit leads that are not confirmed do not belong here. States are NOT stored here: the runner writes them per build identity to the results folder.

entries.title: Model import must not overflow the stack on deeply nested JSON
entries.originalFailure: A 200 KB GLB whose extras nest 100000 levels crashed the importer (exit 0xC00000FD, stack overflow); the JSON parser accepts deep nesting, the recursive URI check did not.
entries.testStrength: Mixed: the nested-URI refusals and the ordinary-model validation are real assertions; the 300000-level case can only fail by crashing the suite (a crash leaves later checks NOT-CHECKED).

entries.title: Plain-cube posed bounds are exact and build/cache no geometry
entries.originalFailure: bounds_at built and cached a new mesh for every changing plain-cube box (tumbling debris), causing about 125000 geometry-cache misses, 370 MB of never-reused meshes and long waits on the cache's exclusive lock in rock-break scenes.
entries.testStrength: Strong for equivalence (500 random poses bit-identical to the mesh walk) and for no geometry built. The performance effect is measured separately (stress runs) and is not asserted by this check.
investigate: HANDOFF-KEYCARD-20261004.md section RESULT: EXACT PLAIN-CUBE BOUNDS

entries.title: Real fracture fragments never fall back to a bounding box
entries.originalFailure: One 1921-point shell shard of a baked statue could not be built as a hull and was replaced by a counted bounding box.
entries.testStrength: Strong for the tested statue; says nothing about other geometry. No runtime speed benefit was demonstrated; do not treat this as a performance fix.

entries.title: A reduced collision hull is never accepted beyond the deviation bound
entries.subsystem: physics hull builder (deep/Physics/PhysicsWorld.cpp BuildHull first-reduction path)
entries.originalFailure: The first reduced hull (more than 256 vertices needed) was returned whatever its error and only counted as over bound.
entries.testStrength: WEAK: dense spheres measure 0.46% against the 0.5% bound, so no input available reached the changed branch. The checks guard the bound property but did not fail on the old code. An injected-bound or adversarial input is still needed.

entries.title: The physics C ABI refuses hostile input instead of passing it to Jolt
entries.originalFailure: Non-finite or zero-quaternion poses, non-positive density, oversized index counts, null arrays, non-finite velocity or platform moves, and removal of a stale body id reached Jolt unchecked.
entries.testStrength: Strong for the refusals it names: with the old code the suite fails at the first EL-07 check, and with the fix all 19 pass and valid calls still succeed. Does not cover EL-07 items it does not list (slp_add_hull poses are covered through AddShape; terrain heights length cannot be checked because the ABI has no length parameter).
investigate: deep/Physics/PhysicsWorld.cpp CheckPose, Add, slp_body_velocity, slp_character_remove, slp_character_platform, slp_character_actor

entries.title: A rope that fails part-way leaves no half-built links
entries.originalFailure: AddCable pushed the cable before its links and constraints existed, so a later failure such as body capacity left unconstrained links in the world and the cable list, ticked every step.
entries.testStrength: Strong for body-capacity failure: with the old code the suite fails at the last EL-08 check (slots not given back); with the fix all four pass. Covers only the capacity failure path, not other throws inside the build.

entries.title: A failed terrain tile cook is reported and recooked instead of ending the process or leaving the tile not ready
entries.originalFailure: A terrain tile cook that throws on its std::async worker ends the process, because the physics module is compiled with _HAS_EXCEPTIONS=0 (Jolt's setting); the audit expected a permanently not-ready tile. A cook failure was never reported or retried.
entries.testStrength: Strong for an injected cook failure on all 36 tiles: they are reported as errors, a later terrain update recooks them and the terrain becomes ready. With the hook but without the guard the process terminated at the first failure (0xC0000409). Real Jolt mesh failures have not been produced; failure is injected through slp_debug_fail_cooks.

entries.title: Failed D3D12 map, reset, close and signal results on the startup and per-frame paths are reported instead of being ignored
entries.originalFailure: Map, command allocator Reset, command list Reset and Close and the per-frame fence Signal results were discarded; after a failure the frame kept recording into a closed or unreset list, wrote through null mapped pointers, or waited on a fence that was never signalled.
entries.testStrength: Strong for the sites that now go through the checked call: each reachable checked result is failed in turn (27 on the reference machine) and must surface as a create or frame error or a cleanup error, with a fresh viewport working afterwards. The hook exists only on the fixed sites, so it cannot show that no other unchecked D3D12 call remains; the unbounded fence wait is unchanged and device-loss behaviour with a real removed device is not tested.
investigate: deep/engine/render_device.h remaining unchecked D3D12 calls and waitFence INFINITE

entries.title: A device failure during viewport destruction is recorded and cannot terminate the process
entries.originalFailure: sl_destroy let flush(), drainRetired or teardown throw out of a noexcept unique_ptr deleter, ending the process instead of reporting the session error.
entries.testStrength: Moderate: a failed fence signal during the destruction flush is injected and must be recorded as a Viewport cleanup error without terminating the process. Only the flush step is injected; failures in the other guarded steps are covered by the guard code but not by a test.
